title: Yaakov Mina’ah (the sectarian)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He belonged to the sect described here as “the known ones” and was a physician in Caesarea, as in [Avodah Zarah 28a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.28a.11). He treated R' Abbahu, who would have been endangered had R' Ami and R' Assi not intervened.[^1][^2]

notes.text: מכת הידועים is literally sect of the known ones; its euphemistic/possibly censored connection to minim is interpretive, without assigning a religion. Mina’ah remains a transliterated sectarian epithet, not a canonical personal/religious binding.

The linked Gemara specifically says the treatment on Rabbi Abbahu’s leg was poisonous and Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi intervened. Hyman’s shorter account reports the danger. His notice locates the physician in Caesarea.
